previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, polymyositis, interstitial lung disease, type 2 diabetes, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and recurrent venous thromboembolism was admitted for a left thigh abscess with fever and pain. She underwent two incision and drainage procedures after imaging confirmed a persistent fluid collection. Treatment included intravenous antibiotics, later transitioned to oral Augmentin and Bactrim. During her stay, she was found to have a polymyositis flare with elevated CK, managed with IV and then oral steroids, tapering to 10 mg prednisone. Her warfarin had been stopped prior to admission due to heavy menstrual bleeding, leading to a subtherapeutic INR; it was restarted and increased to 7 mg daily. Acute on chronic heart failure was managed with a short course of IV furosemide. Vaginal bleeding was evaluated with a normal pelvic ultrasound and attributed to PCOS or fibroids, possibly exacerbated by anticoagulation. She improved clinically, with normalizing labs, and was discharged home on a completed antibiotic course, adjusted anticoagulation, and rheumatology follow-up for immunosuppressive medication reinitiation.
problems: Cutaneous abscess of left lower limb
Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  US EXTREMITY LIMITED SOFT TISSUE RIGHT

INDICATION:  ___ yo F PMHx obesity, DVT/PE on Coumadin who presents with fever
and right groin pain, found to have abscess in ED s/p I D.  Still significant
pain and induration on exam, please assess for ongoing abscess// Abscess?

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale ultrasound images were obtained of the superficial
tissues of the right groin.

COMPARISON:  None

FINDINGS: 

Transverse and sagittal images were obtained of the superficial tissues of the
right groin.  Deep to the drainage site, there is a 3.3 x 1.4 x 2.0 cm
heterogeneous collection with surrounding hyperemia, consistent with abscess. 
There is overlying subcutaneous edema.


IMPRESSION: 

3.3 x 1.4 x 2.0 cm right groin abscess.

EXAMINATION:  Ultrasound guided drainage

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with right groin abscess, please drain if
possible// aspiration drainage

COMPARISON:
Ultrasound dated earlier same day.

PROCEDURE:  Ultrasound-guided drainage of right groin collection.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___, radiology trainee and Dr. ___,
attending radiologist. Dr. ___ supervised the trainee during the
key components of the procedure and reviewed and agree with the trainee's
findings.

TECHNIQUE:  The risks, benefits, and alternatives of the procedure were
explained to the patient.  After a detailed discussion, informed written
consent was obtained.  A pre-procedure timeout using three patient identifiers
was performed per ___ protocol.

The patient was placed in a supine position on the US scan table. Limited
preprocedure ultrasound was performed to localize the collection.  Based on
the ultrasound findings an appropriate skin entry site for the aspiration was
chosen.  The site was marked.  Local anesthesia was administered with 1%
Lidocaine solution.

Using continuous sonographic guidance, an 18 gauge spinal needle was advanced
into the collection.  Approximately 1 cc of blood was aspirated and sent for
microbiology evaluation.  The needle was removed and sterile dressing was
applied.

The procedure was tolerated well, and there were no immediate post-procedural
complications.

SEDATION:  None

FINDINGS: 

Heterogeneous right groin collection was targeted, though only a small amount
of blood was aspirated.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful US-guided drainage of 1 cc of blood from the collection though
several different portions of the collection were stuck.
